title: Surgical regional cutover and controlled traffic migration for hosted API
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Goal: Harden the hosted API deployment pipeline to support surgical regional cutovers, deterministic traffic migration, and strong upgrade gating. This ticket covers designing the traffic shift orchestration, adding deterministic rollout gates (health + quality metrics), implementing a regional failover path, and producing tooling to execute controlled blue->green swaps with per-region hysteresis and safety timeouts. Motivation: Recent partial rollouts revealed uneven cache priming, KV cache mismatch, and latency spikes when 30-50% traffic hit new model variants in us-east. We need a safer, repeatable process that integrates health checks, automated validation against baseline prompts, and rollback hooks that run without operator intervention.
acceptance_criteria: A rollout can be executed for a single region with an automated staged traffic curve (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and configurable hold windows
Circuit-breaker triggers defined and implemented: API error rate > 0.5% OR 95th latency regression > 25% OR quality regression > 1.5% on golden prompt set
Automated baseline evaluation runs during holds and fails fast if quality gates do not pass
Rollback path completes in under 90s with no dropped requests and preserves token accounting
Runbook and console controls added: 'surgical cutover' button, live progress viz, and one-click rollback
End-to-end smoke tests and an integration test in CI that simulates regional failure and validates failover routing
tasks: Spec: document rollout state machine and gating thresholds in Confluence (link below)
Implement staged traffic controller that speaks to routing plane and operator API
Add quality regression harness that runs golden prompt set against candidate region build
Hook controller to console: progress UI + manual override + audit logging
Ensure KV cache warmup strategy and prefix-preserving priming to avoid cold-latency spikes
Add automated canary analysis job in CI with synthetic load for each release
Run a dry-run in canary region and capture metrics dashboards for postmortem

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive traffic curves shorten blast radius time but increase risk of cache cold start effects. We will default to conservative holds and allow project-level override for advanced operators.

We intentionally separate quality gate (semantic correctness) from infra gate (latency/errors). Both must pass to advance; infra failures trigger immediate rollback, quality failures trigger hold + human review by PM/ML engineer.
Rollout tooling must be idempotent: repeated apply of the same traffic curve should be a no-op and produce deterministic audit entries.
Consider future extension: tie rollout decisions to model LTS channel tags (e.g., lts-2026.q1) so customers on LTS are not auto-rolled to experimental variants.

SRE to own emergency-mode where traffic is diverted to warm standby region for 15 minutes while investigation happens. Implementation detail: BGP-level routing + internal DNS TTL manipulation planned but out-of-scope for this ticket.
